prose: cutover_guard.bash, green at 125f601d on its narrower corpus and refusing after the prune by design; the criterion is satisfied by the repo-wide measurement on it.
note:
Driven by vc 2026-08-30 on dc's build (125f601d), verified by a route independent of the guard: `intent/plugins/claude/bin/` now holds `intent_claude_cwi` alone and `lib/` holds `critic_runner.sh` + `rules_lib.sh`, with no `bin/intent` source or exec edge among them. Guard exit 0, partition closes 1 driven + 14 static-only = 15 of 15. **THE ANTI-VACUITY ARM IS WHAT MAKES THE GREEN MEAN ANYTHING AND THIS WAS THE RUN WHERE IT COULD HAVE MATTERED**: cwi survives the prune carrying its own primitives, so the control still reconstructs a pre-port form and still requires it to break -- a prune that emptied the population would have printed the same ok line over nothing. Moved by vc rather than dc because dc holds WP-12 and that is the shape where a node scores its own row.

**RED 2026-09-01 08:40Z (vc). THE GREEN WAS TRUE ABOUT A NARROWER CORPUS THAN THE CRITERION, AND vc IS THE ONE WHO MOVED IT.** Found by dc, driving the bats suite hv ran: 1282 pass, 193 fail, and **186 of the 193 are ONE cause** -- `error: Plugin command not found` for the four `intent_claude_*` scripts deleted at `125f601d` under this very criterion's authorised prune. The tool is right and the tests drive something that is gone.

**THE CRITERION'S OWN SENTENCE IS UNMET.** It reads _nothing in the repo EXECUTES or EMITS a `bin/` intent script path_, and its reasoning turns on _their only executor is `bin/intent`, which the cut removes_. **`bin/intent` HAS NOT BEEN REMOVED** -- re-driven by vc: present, executable, 11152 bytes, answering, with 26 v2 `intent*` scripts beside it. **The prune took the SIX LEAVES and left the TRUNK, and the trunk still dispatches to the holes.** And the largest executor in the repo is the test estate itself: `tests/lib/test_helper.bash:21` sets `INTENT_BIN` to that path and `:148` execs it, for **113 `.bats` files**.

**WHY THIS ROW'S EVIDENCE COULD NOT SEE IT, AND THE POPULATION IS THE WHOLE DEFECT.** The evidence above names `intent/plugins/claude/bin/` and `lib/`. **Every word of it is TRUE and its corpus is narrower than the criterion it scores** -- vc's own recorded class, measuring something true and ruling on something wider, committed by vc in the act of taking the row off dc to avoid a self-scored one.

**AND THE ANTI-VACUITY ARM WAS NEVER GOING TO CATCH IT.** It proves the guard can still FIRE; it says nothing about whether the guard can SEE. **A CONTROL AGAINST VACUITY IS NOT A CONTROL AGAINST A NARROW CORPUS** -- the first asks whether the instrument can ever say no, the second asks whether it is looking at the right thing, **and passing the first is exactly what stops anyone asking the second.**

**THE CRITERION IS NOT REWORDED**, on vc's own standing ruling from `AC-06.3`: a criterion is not reworded to what the current state satisfies. The bar is reachable -- under hv's feature-complete ruling the trunk goes, and the sentence becomes true when it does. **TO GO GREEN AGAIN THIS ROW'S POPULATION MUST INCLUDE `tests/`** -- every repo-resident executor of a `bin/` intent path, not two plugin directories. Ruled by vc, built by dc, as part of the row moving rather than before it.

**FIGURE CORRECTED 2026-09-01 08:43Z, AND IT WAS WRONG IN THE NOTE THAT ASSERTS RIGOUR ABOUT POPULATIONS.** The `113` above is vc's and it is not the number. **vc COUNTED UNDER `tests/` WHEN THE CRITERION SAYS `the repo`** -- the same narrowing this entry exists to record, committed inside the correction of it, one paragraph after naming the class. dc reported `114` and was closer.

**RE-DRIVEN REPO-WIDE, AND THE CRITERION HAS TWO VERBS WITH TWO DIFFERENT POPULATIONS** (dc, who caught that `EXECUTES or EMITS` is not one set here; both figures re-driven by vc). **115 tracked `.bats`, 114 real** -- the odd one is `bin/.devbin/lib/tmpl/test.bats`, a VENDORED TEMPLATE under an integrity manifest rather than a test. **EMITS is 114**: `test_helper.bash:21` resolves `bin/intent` and EXPORTS it, so every file loading the helper carries the path in its environment whether it ever runs it or not. **EXECUTES is 85, BY TWO ROUTES** -- 78 through the `run_intent` dispatcher and 35 straight at `${INTENT_BIN_DIR}/intent_<sub>`, overlapping. (dc measured the direct route at 31 against vc's 35 on a wider pattern; **the UNION is 85 either way**, so the disagreement lies inside the overlap and moves nothing.)

**SO THE POPULATION THIS ROW MUST COVER IS NOT ONE NUMBER AND A SINGLE TOTAL IS WHAT LET THE LAST GUARD LOOK COMPLETE.** The rebuilt guard reports both verbs separately and both execution routes separately. **THE DIRECT ROUTE IS THE ONE THAT GOES MISSING**, and `test_helper.bash:15-18` already warns about it in its own words -- _`INTENT_BIN_DIR` is NOT a substitute ... the ~146 `${INTENT_BIN_DIR}/intent_<sub>` call sites invoke those directly, bypassing the `bin/intent` dispatcher._ **The trap is documented in the file the guard has to read.**

**AND dc's THIRD QUESTION IS THE KEEPER, BECAUSE NEITHER OF THE FIRST TWO REACHES IT.** Vacuity asks _can this instrument ever say no_. Corpus asks _is it looking at the right thing_. **FORM asks _does the SUBJECT have more than one shape_** -- and AT-12.1 could have been pointed at `tests/`, fired correctly, and still missed 35 files, because the corpus would have been right and the PATTERN wrong. **Passing either of the first two is exactly what stops you asking the third.** -- RETIRED at the 3.0.1 cut (vc): after the prune cutover_guard.bash exits 2, NO FILE WAS CONTROLLED, by design. bin/intent_helpers is gone, so the call-edge arm is n/a, and neither driven survivor carries a bin/ primitive of its own, so no control arm can run. The instrument ended with its subject. The criterion's sentence was measured directly over the repo, tests/ included, and is satisfied by that evidence.
